results.claim: At the advertised knight-encounter staging configuration, the idealized ambiguous move has the two global possibilities ±r, and both stated branches are exclusive and end in K(q+r;a,r,f).
results.proof_sketch: Let (T,H,B)=(q+r,q+2r,q+2r+f), with a,r,f orthogonal signed unit vectors, and define K(p;a,r,f)={p,p+a,p+2r+f}. Among the 48 signed-coordinate transformations, those fixing the colored-neighbor direction −f and wall direction −a form a two-element stabilizer whose orbit on r is {r,−r}. First H enters B's old node while B moves to q+r+f or q+3r+f. In the −r branch, the next round sends T to q+r+a, B to q+r, and H to q+3r+f. In the +r branch, H first moves to q+r+f; the following round sends H to q+r and T to q+r+a while B remains at q+3r+f. Both endpoints are {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f). Exact enumeration found only unit or idle moves, distinct same-round destinations, and no oppositely traversed edge. This proves only the idealized positional macro.

results.claim: From the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, the distinct-choice branch gives D(q;d,e,f), while the contact-and-rotation branch gives D(q;e,d,f), without a collision or edge swap.
results.proof_sketch: Let d and e be the two distinct directions in {a,−r}, define D(p;u,v,w)={p,p+u,p+v+w}, and start from {q,q+d,q+f}. In the distinct-choice branch, the third robot moves from q+f to q+e+f, giving D(q;d,e,f). In the contact branch, it first reaches q+d+f. The stated rotation then moves the occupants of q and q+d to q+e and q, respectively, giving {q,q+e,q+d+f}=D(q;e,d,f). Orthogonality makes every indicated non-idle displacement a unit grid edge. The destinations are distinct, and the rotation edges q→q+e and q+d→q are neither equal nor oppositely oriented copies of one edge. This proves only the positional branch effects, not their reachability or realization by colored local-view rules.

results.claim: From the advertised outer-reset conversion staging configuration, every choice of d, x and the ±d conversion branch is exclusive and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
results.proof_sketch: Let h=−f; choose d from {a,−r}, let e be the other direction, choose x from {e,h}, and let y be the other member of {e,h}. After the advertised follower shift, label the positions s, s+d, and s+d+x by L, M, and C. The conversion moves M to C's old position and C by ±d. In the +d branch, correcting M to s+x gives {s,s+x,s+2d+x}. In the −d branch, correcting M to s+2d+x gives the same set, although C rather than M then occupies s+x. Finally, send whichever robot occupies s+x to s while L moves from s to s+y. The endpoint is {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Exact enumeration over every advertised choice found only unit or idle displacements, distinct same-round destinations, and no edge swap. This remains an unlabeled positional lemma and establishes no compatible shade transitions.

results.claim: The three retained positional macros do not define or prove a visibility-one algorithm with at most 76 shades.
results.proof_sketch: The source requires an algorithm A=(Cl,Init,T), where Cl is a finite shade set, Init maps every eligible grid to a nonempty set of initial configurations, and T maps every local view to a movement and next shade. The retained lemmas describe only finitely many uncolored geometric branches from assumed staging configurations. They specify neither Cl nor Init nor T, and they do not prove consistency on local-view orbits, reachability of the staging configurations, termination under every adversarial transformation sequence, preservation of global invariants, or perpetual coverage of every eligible grid. Hence they are only conditional positional calculations, not an at-most-76-shade construction or a demonstrated step toward one.

results.claim: Neither alternative in the target is established.
results.proof_sketch: The construction alternative requires an actual ambiguous visibility-one tuple (Cl,Init,T) for exactly three Batdroids using at most 76 shades, together with a proof that every permitted execution perpetually visits every vertex of every grid whose side lengths are at least four. The preceding insufficiency result shows that no such construction is supplied. The optimality alternative requires a lower bound excluding every algorithm using at most 76 shades; no retained result supplies such a bound. Therefore neither target alternative is established.

final_writeup:
Revision outcome: the open target remains unresolved; no material partial progress on either requested alternative is established.

The first three results preserve the verified conditional coordinate calculations. At the advertised knight-encounter staging configuration, the two idealized branches are exclusive and converge to K(q+r;a,r,f). At the ordinary-transition staging configuration, the two idealized branches produce D(q;d,e,f) and D(q;e,d,f). At the advertised outer-reset conversion staging configuration, both ±d branches are exclusive and converge to K(s;y,d,x). Exact integer enumeration checks these finite traces over all 48 signed frames. These are ancillary, uncolored positional calculations. No result connects them to a shade reduction, proves their staging configurations reachable in a candidate algorithm, or realizes them through a compatible total transition function. They are therefore not claimed as material progress on the target.

The construction alternative requires an ambiguous visibility-one algorithm A=(Cl,Init,T) for exactly three Batdroids with |Cl|≤76 and a proof that every permitted execution perpetually explores every eligible grid. The retained results provide none of Cl, Init, or T; no colored local-view-orbit consistency proof; no staging-reachability or macro-composition invariant; no adversarial termination argument; and no universal coverage proof. The source supplies a 77-shade construction, not an at-most-76-shade construction.

The optimality alternative requires a universal lower bound excluding every ambiguous algorithm with at most 76 shades. No retained result gives such a bound. The source impossibility theorem excludes well-defined visibility-one algorithms for three Batdroids regardless of color count, whereas the target permits ambiguous algorithms; hence that theorem does not prove 77-shade optimality.

Accordingly, neither target alternative is established and claimed_resolution is NONE. All five verified claim wordings are retained. The phrase calling the macros “material positional lemmas” is narrowed to “conditional positional calculations,” because no bridge from those traces to either target alternative has been proved.
